text:
maria: hey - heads up, my onboarding sample app started failing only on edge deployments after I touched package.json. works in node but throws in Vercel/Edge. :facepalm:

ashish: what error do you see? stack? package.json?

maria: main error: `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` when the edge runtime tries to hydrate. Full log:```
Error: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at instantiateModule (internal/modules/esm/loader:xxx)
    at async loadESM (internal/process/esm_loader:yyy)
```

maria: package.json snippet:```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/sample-sdk",
  "version": "0.3.2",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  },
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

ashish: hmm - bundlers on edge (and SWC + ESM resolver) appear to prefer `module`/`import` entry. If the runtime expects a CJS-compatible bundle (some edge runtimes do for now), the ESM file might be shipped verbatim and break. Also TS server sometimes can't follow conditional exports to `types` if paths aren't mirrored.

sam: do we publish both bundles to npm? are source maps included?

maria: yes both bundles are in the tarball and sourcemaps included. The surprising bit was TypeScript in the sample app couldn't resolve the types when using the package via workspace reference — tsc fell back to the `module` entry and couldn't find corresponding declarations for some helper files.

kevin: saw a customer report similar: Next.js edge function using our SDK failed after they upgraded to 0.3.x. It worked on serverless node runtime but errored only on edge.

ashish: short-term workaround: remove `module` from package.json so bundlers pick `main` (CJS) or add an explicit `exports."./package.json"` types entry. Another hack is adding a `browser` field pointing to the CJS-ish bundle for edge builds. Not great though.

maria: confirmed: nuking "module" in node_modules locally fixed the edge build. Verified with Vercel deploy preview — success. :tada:

sam: that's a fragile fix. Long-term we should publish a dual-resolved package with mirrored typings: every conditional export that points to an entry should expose a parallel `types` path or use `typesVersions` so TS can map ESM -> d.ts.

ashish: agreed. Action items I propose:
- update publish pipeline to output a small `exports` map that includes `"types"` sub-entries (or `exports."./types"` mapping) for each conditional target
- add an integration test: install package in a fresh Next/Vercel edge project and run `vercel dev` smoke test
- update sample-app onboarding docs to recommend the compatible bundler target / flag

maria: adding: also include a fallthrough `.` -> `dist/index.cjs.js` for older runtimes (put under `require`) and keep `import` for modern ones. And update CHANGELOG to call out the break.

kevin: can we fast-track a patch release? customers are hitting this in prod.

ashish: I'll open a GH issue and a patch branch today. created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2345 (devx-bot attached)

devx-bot: Issue created: redwood-inference/sdk#2345 — "packages: modules field + exports map cause edge/ts resolution failures" (assigned: ashish) :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks. I'll add repro steps from the sample app and include the Vercel logs in the issue.

sam: also adding a small CI job to smoke test with `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-modules` and a minimal SWC build to catch regressions going forward.

kevin: thanks team — customers appreciate the rapid response. :heart:
